title: POC scoping - cost modeling with Lumina Health
summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics for a chart-summarization assistant: per-token estimates, batching and KV/prefix caching, sample throughput targets, and timelines for benchmarks and pilot Dedicated capacity. Security and HIPAA considerations were discussed; next steps include sharing a detailed cost model spreadsheet and scheduling benchmark runs.

Ethan to schedule end-to-end benchmark run with Lumina sample prompts on 2026-04-29
Redwood to share SOC 2 and HIPAA alignment docs (link in chat)
Lumina to provide PII-free sample dataset and success criteria by 2026-04-28

Ethan Chen - Set up benchmark run + collection scripts; request sample prompt set - due 2026-04-29

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Sara Nguyen (Lumina, Head of ML), Carlos Rios (Lumina Platform), Priya Kapoor (Lumina Security), Jared Mills (Lumina Product)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick agenda - cost modeling, how we'll size the POC, success criteria, and timeline. Ethan will cover benchmark details.
00:28 Dr. Sara: Thanks, Maya. We're mainly trying to understand what the per-token and per-request economics look like for our chart-summarization assistant. We get variable-length notes, lots of tokens, and we care about both latency and cost.
00:45 Maya: Totally. One thing to call out up front: for POC we usually run both hosted and a short Dedicated trial so you can see end-to-end numbers and also a production-shaped throughput.
01:12 Ethan: Quick clarification - are you doing single-turn summarization or multi-turn with context retention? That changes KV cache behavior.
01:28 Dr. Sara: Mostly single-turn but we want to keep prior note embeddings for reranking; and for follow-ups we expect sequence lengths up to 3k tokens.
01:45 Carlos: And our target SLA is 95th percentile under 600ms for the UI path, but we're willing to relax that during POC if cost savings are significant.
02:05 Priya: On security, HIPAA is a hard requirement. We'll need encryption, KMS, audit logs, and an option for VPC/private deployment; want to see SOC 2 artifacts.
02:25 Maya: We'll share the security pack after the call - Ethan, remind me the link in chat?
02:34 Ethan: Yep, dropping link to SOC2 + HIPAA whitepaper in the chat.
02:40 Jared: Also, timeline - we'd like to decide on approach in two weeks; pilot starting early May would be ideal.
03:02 Maya: Great. Let's walk through the cost model assumptions. High level: tokens-in + tokens-out per request, batching effects, and prefix/KV cache hit rates. For our estimate we use a per-token runtime cost baseline that maps to instance/GPU-hour and inferred token throughput.
03:35 Ethan: For example, on gpus we typically see X tokens per second per GPU for the model we recommended - for the POC model (redwood-llm-1-small, note: placeholder) an unbatched 1k-token request runs ~ 150ms per token? Sorry, I mean 150 ms total for 1k-token generation on a 4xA100 equiv - transcription error - actual numbers will be in the spreadsheet.
04:05 Dr. Sara: You just said 150ms per token which is...
04:08 Ethan: Sorry, ran together - 150ms total for that gen in our rough example. Point is batching dramatically changes unit cost.
04:20 Carlos: Can you explain batching and its impact? We saw in prior work that async batching can reduce costs but increase tail latency.
04:36 Ethan: Exactly. Continuous batching groups requests into micro-batches; you amortize kernel launch and KV cache overhead. In our cost model we show three knobs: target batch size, max wait window (ms), and smart routing to dedicated capacity.
05:05 Maya: And caching - prefix/KV caching reduces repeated context work. For chart summaries, if multiple notes share a template or repeated sections, cache hit rates can be 20-60% which reduces per-request compute by that factor. We'll include scenarios: low (10%), medium (30%), high (50%) cache hit.
05:38 Dr. Sara: How do you model per-token pricing for hosted vs Dedicated? We have a rough monthly budget - $15k initially.
05:50 Maya: Hosted is usage-based (per-token + per-embedding). Dedicated is committed capacity - monthly fee plus lower per-token compute cost. For short POC we can provide a fixed trial Dedicated allocation to measure. The spreadsheet will show break-even points based on tokens/day.
06:15 Carlos: Sample workload - we have 20k summaries/day, average input 1.2k tokens, output 220 tokens. Peak concurrency ~60 RPS.
06:32 Ethan: Perfect, that feeds directly into batching math. At 60 RPS, with a 20ms wait window and average batch size 8-12, your effective per-token cost drops ~ 30-50% compared to no-batch.
06:53 Priya: Any concerns about PII? We'll strip PII for the POC dataset but need to validate encryption at rest and in transit.
07:05 Maya: We'll confirm encryption, KMS integration, and provide redacted sample options.
07:20 Jared: Benchmarks - we want a real run against our sample to measure latency distribution, token costs, and quality regressions. What does that look like operationally?
07:35 Ethan: We'll run three benchmark phases: 1) Synthetic local runs to validate model/latency; 2) End-to-end run with your sample dataset on Hosted; 3) Dedicated trial run with same dataset. We'll collect token counts, latency histograms, and quality metrics (ROUGE/QA checks).
08:02 Dr. Sara: Quality metrics - we need to ensure the quantized variants don't regress. Do you provide regression thresholds?
08:14 Ethan: Yes, we'll set explicit thresholds tied to your eval set; if quantized model causes >5% drop on key metrics we flag it.
08:26 Maya: On timelines: if you provide sample prompts by 4/28, we can run hosted benchmarks 4/29-4/30 and start Dedicated trial 5/4 for two weeks. Decision deadline early May as requested.
08:42 Carlos: That works. Back to the numbers - can you give a ballpark per-token for our workload?
08:50 Maya: Ballpark hosted: $0.0009 - $0.002 per input token and $0.0012 - $0.0028 per output token depending on model size and batching. With your distribution (1.2k in / 220 out) that maps to roughly $0.15 - $0.6 per summary. Dedicated mid-sized pool could halve that.
09:22 Dr. Sara: Half seems attractive. How sensitive is that to batch window? If we reduce wait window to meet latency SLA, cost goes up?
09:31 Ethan: Yes. Example: 20ms wait window vs 80ms can change batch size from ~4 to ~14, and per-token compute cost moves correspondingly. We'll include sensitivity analysis in the spreadsheet.
10:00 Maya: Also, KV/prefix cache hit reduces token work - if you get 30% cache hit on prefix, your cost per summary drops by roughly the same percent of generation compute. But there's cache memory tradeoffs; Dedicated pools give you more predictable KV storage.
10:30 Priya: For Dedicated, we need to confirm VPC peering and audit log export to our SIEM. Is that supported?
10:38 Ethan: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and audit exports; we'll add the config docs to the security pack.
10:50 Dr. Sara: On benchmarks, can we test with a mix of short and long notes? Our distribution is heavy-tailed.
10:57 Ethan: Definitely. We'll run a 90/10 mix as well as your actual empirical distribution. That will capture tail effects on batching and latency.
11:18 Jared: Any recommendation on model variant? We're currently prototyping with an off-the-shelf 13B model.
11:25 Ethan: For POC we often recommend a 7-13B quantized variant for cost/latency balance; we can test 7B quantized vs 13B q4 and measure quality delta. The cost spreadsheet will show unit costs for each.
12:00 Dr. Sara: About embeddings: we do reranking and retrieval; are embedding costs separate in the model?
12:07 Maya: Yes embeddings are billed separately. We can include an amortized embedding cost per request based on how often you refresh embeddings.
12:20 Carlos: Operational question - if we go Dedicated, do we still get the same fallback to hosted in spikes?
12:28 Ethan: Yes, we support smart routing/fallback. You can set policy to overflow to hosted or to a warm standby Dedicated pool. That helps with burst handling without overprovisioning.
12:45 Priya: For compliance, we need a data flow diagram and retention settings.
12:52 Maya: We'll include that in the security pack.
13:05 Dr. Sara: Can you walk through an example cost calculation for a single summary?
13:12 Ethan: Sure: assume input 1,200 tokens, output 220 tokens. Model computes on both input and output; total tokens 1,420. With batching and cache, effective compute tokens might be 1,020. If hosted per-token is $0.0012 on average, cost = 1,020 * 0.0012 = $1.224 per summary - that's a high example; with Dedicated and batching maybe $0.45. We'll add lower-range examples; my numbers are illustrative only.
14:05 Maya: Note those numbers are sensitive; spreadsheet will show median, p50/p95 ranges.
14:20 Dr. Sara: We'll need to show leadership a conservative case and an optimistic case.
14:28 Maya: Agreed. We'll provide low/medium/high scenarios with assumptions listed.
14:40 Carlos: How do we instrument to collect token counts accurately?
14:48 Ethan: We'll provide client-side hooks and server-side token accounting that logs token-in/token-out per request. For the POC we'll enable extended logs for a small subset and aggregate metrics.
15:10 Priya: Is there any risk of data leaving our region? We need region control for PHI.
15:17 Maya: Hosted can be regional; Dedicated gives more control. We'll show region placement options in the security pack.
15:30 Jared: On success criteria - what does Redwood need from Lumina to mark POC success?
15:36 Maya: Typically: 1) Meet quality thresholds on your eval set (<=5% regression), 2) Demonstrate unit economics within your target budget ($15k/mo equivalent), 3) Latency SLOs met for 95th under an agreed relaxed threshold, 4) No outstanding security blockers.
16:00 Dr. Sara: That's reasonable. For budget, is $15k/mo realistic for our 20k/day?
16:07 Ethan: It depends on effective batching/caching and model choice. The spreadsheet will have a break-even chart; for 20k/day and good batching, $15k/mo could be tight but possible with Dedicated and aggressive caching.
16:35 Maya: Ok, let's capture tentative timeline: 4/28 deliver dataset and prompts, 4/29-hosted benchmark, 5/4 start Dedicated trial for two weeks, checkpoint 5/18 to review.
16:50 Carlos: We'll aim to get prompts to you by 4/28.
17:05 Priya: I'll review the security pack and flag anything critical.
17:15 Ethan: One nuance - our quantized kernels have different perf profiles for long sequences; we'll include kernel selection recommendations. (note: 'kernels' sometimes transcribed as 'cernel' in older notes)
17:40 Dr. Sara: Can the benchmark include cost-per-conversation as well as per-summary? We want both.
17:46 Ethan: Yes, we'll compute both aggregate and per-conversation costs.
18:05 Maya: Quick question from chat - Redwood support for customer-managed keys (HSM)?
18:12 Ethan: Yes, KMS and HSM integrations are supported for Private/Dedicated; details in the security doc.
18:30 Jared: Are there any hidden fees or egress concerns?
18:35 Maya: Egress might be charged depending on region and if you pull large datasets; we'll call that out. No opaque surcharge - everything in spreadsheet.
19:00 Dr. Sara: Ok, I'm comfortable with the plan. We'll provide the dataset and success criteria.
19:10 Maya: Awesome. Final recap for next steps: Maya sends spreadsheet and pricing, Ethan schedules benchmark and shares scripts, Lumina provides sample dataset and security requirements. We'll aim for decisions early May.
19:35 (brief cross-talk)
19:50 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription has a few typical errors (numbers and ms figures were verbal and clarified). Shared artifacts referenced: "Cost model spreadsheet" (link sent in chat), "SOC2 + HIPAA whitepaper" (link), benchmark script repo (link).
